title: engine:F5 — Persistent containment, portal, and licensed item-pool state
description:
Persist per-instance containment and portal ownership, and licensed random /
card-pool state, across every item operation.

ROOT CAUSE: item custody and persistent-state primitives exist, but the complete
containment / portal / card-pool execution contract has no exact owner. These
items carry state that must survive transfer, attunement change, and
destruction — what is inside a container, which portal instance is linked to
which, and which cards have already been drawn from a specific deck instance.
Modeling them as ordinary item state loses the per-instance identity.

LEDGER ROW: capabilityId engine:F5, primitive
"containment-portal-and-card-pool-instance-state".
Pack membership: records whose projected data.executionReadiness hooks qualify as
engine:F5 with containment, portal, or card-pool semantics, compared against the
source inventory clauses named by the 2026-07-24 audit.

CROSSES: engine:F3 (owned-entity lifecycle) and engine:F1 (seeded deterministic
selection — a card draw must be reproducible under replay). engine:F5 owns it.

REQUIRED INVARIANT: per-instance state is identity-bearing and survives custody
change. Two instances of the same item key never share pool, containment, or
portal state. Draws are seeded and replayable.

NOTE: consult the existing item-adoption quarantine gates before adding any
fail-closed precondition here — a resolution path blocked by the same gate it is
meant to clear is a known deadlock shape in this codebase.

PROVENANCE: this bead exists because the bootstrap capability ledger
(eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1, PR #477) found this primitive had NO owner in the current
family decomposition. It was recorded there as ownershipStatus=proposed-new-bead;
this bead is that proposal made real, and the ledger row now points here.

CROSS-FAMILY PRIMITIVE. The owning family is named in the title, but the
requirement crosses family boundaries. Per the authorization criteria on
eshyra-olc5.1, a cross-family primitive is named ONCE and assigned ONE owning
family — do not re-implement it under the families it touches. Coordinate
instead.

SEQUENCING: this bead is blocked by its family's decomposition task and must not
be started before it. Decomposition does not RE-CREATE this bead; it reconciles
against it, decides whether the primitive splits further, and names the
conformance scenarios. Duplicating it under a sibling family is the failure mode
to avoid.

GREEN BAR: the nine-point definition on eshyra-o9bd.19 applies — this primitive
is not done until a provider-neutral implementation exists, reference-engine
conformance tests exercise the committed PACK representation (not a fixture),
tool exposure and state mutation are correct, unsupported input fails CLOSED,
and replay / deterministic equivalence holds where applicable.

COUNT HYGIENE: membership comes from the ledger's generated query for this
primitive. Never hand-copy a hook count into an acceptance test.

*** engine:F* IS A QUALIFIED PREFIX. engine:F1..F10 are the pack's
executionReadiness engineHooks families — NOT the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t's
different F1-F10, and NOT the fable:F1..F8 audit findings.
acceptance_criteria:
• Containment, portal, and pool state are per-instance and identity-bearing, never shared across instances of one item key.
• State survives transfer, attunement change, and custody transitions.
• Pool draws are seeded and reproduce exactly under replay.
• Conformance tests drive the contract from the committed pack representation.
• Unsupported input fails CLOSED without corrupting instance state.
• The engine:F5 ledger membership query returns zero unowned clauses for this primitive.
